Built-in Slash Commands ​

These commands are used to manage your CodeBuddy Code sessions. Here is the current support status:

Command Parameters CodeBuddy Support Description
/help ✅ Supported Display help information and provide guidance on feedback channels.
/agents ✅ Supported Manage built-in and custom AI agents; view the effective routing values and their sources for built-in sub-agents, and save model settings to Global or Project scope. Specific scenario models can be viewed in /model. Use /agent-mode to switch the current session's main Agent mode.
/branch [name] ✅ Supported Create a branch at the current conversation point, carrying over the main Agent mode, model, output style, and additional directories, and automatically switch to it. Branching is not yet supported for conversations that contain subagent history. Optionally specify a branch name.
/config [list | get | set] ✅ Supported View or modify local configuration. Opens an interactive panel when used without parameters, list lists current settings, get <key> reads a setting, set <key> <value> modifies a setting.
/model [list | model-name] ✅ Supported Switch or view the main model. Opens an interactive interface when used without parameters. list lists available models; when provided with a model name, directly switches the main model. Switching is rejected while a task is running. If the context exceeds the target model's window, a standard /compact runs first; the switch is rejected only if the context still does not fit after compaction.
/model:lite [list | model-id] ✅ Supported Switch or view the effective model and source for the lite scenario variant (used by lightweight subtasks like Explore). Opens an interactive selection interface when used without parameters (including Global / Project settings), list lists available models, or directly switches when provided with a model ID.
/fork [name] ✅ Supported Alias for /branch. Copies active conversation history, carries over session settings, and automatically switches to the new branch. Conversations containing subagent history show a not-yet-supported notice. Use /resume to return to the original conversation.
